newsitem.title: UK: UK's Channel 4 welcomes end to funding formula.
newsitem.headline: UK's Channel 4 welcomes end to funding formula.

text.p: Britain's Channel 4 television station on Monday welcomed the government's move to end its current funding formula for the channel and said it would spend more money on commissioning original British programmes and on further training of staff.
Earlier on Monday, Britain's Department of Trade & Industry said the current government funding formula used to run Channel 4 would end in 1999.

The DTI quoted British culture secretary Chris Smith as saying that there was no need, or real justification for the C4 formula now that it was a well-established broadcaster with a steady income stream.

Channel 4's chief executive Michael Jackson said that although the current funding formula would continue until the start of 1999, the channel would still have an extra 25 million stg more to spend on programmes in 1998.
"I am pleased that this settlement will enable us to proceed wholeheartedly with our plans for new digital services," Jackson said.

Channel 4 was founded in 1982 and was originally financed by a levy on the advertising revenue of all of Britain's commercial independent television companies. In return, the companies sold Channel 4's advertising time and kept the proceeds.
But in 1993, Channel 4 became a public corporation, licensed and regulated by the ITC and funded by selling its own advertising time.
